title: Article 379 — Provisions as to provisional Parliament (Omitted)

content.overview: Article 379 provided for the provisional Parliament (the Constituent Assembly functioning as provisional Parliament) until both Houses were duly constituted. It was omitted by the Constitution (Seventh Amendment) Act, 1956, s. 29 and Schedule (w.e.f. 1 November 1956) after the transitional purpose was spent.
content.glance: Art 379 omitted by 7th Amendment 1956 (w.e.f. 1-11-1956). Provisional Parliament transitional provision — spent.
content.study:
Articles 379–391 were temporary provisions in Part XXI for the transition from Dominion to Republic and the first elected Parliament and State legislatures.

Omission: Constitution (Seventh Amendment) Act, 1956, s. 29 and Schedule (w.e.f. 1-11-1956).

Examination rule: Do not cite Article 379 (or 380–391) as living law. They are spent transitional provisions.

sections.heading: Constitutional status
sections.body: Omitted by the 7th Amendment, 1956 (w.e.f. 1-11-1956). The provisional Parliament operated from commencement until the first elected Houses were constituted; the articles then became redundant.

questionsAndAnswers.question: What is the status of Article 379?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Article 379 was omitted by the Constitution (Seventh Amendment) Act, 1956 (w.e.f. 1-11-1956). It was a spent transitional provision for the provisional Parliament.

examTips: Treat Arts 379–391 as a single transitional block omitted by the 7th Amendment.
content.migrationNote: Remediated 2026-10-09: accurate 7th Amendment omission of provisional Parliament provision.

authoritativeSources: Constitution (Seventh Amendment) Act, 1956, s. 29 and Sch.
keyTakeaways: Art 379 omitted by 7th Amendment, 1956; provisional Parliament transitional — spent.
